question.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthogonal?

I. $U=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $V=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $W=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
$\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2},{u}_{3}\},$ 
$\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\},$ and 
$\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2}\},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0,\,{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3}=0,\,{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3}=0.$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0.$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-1+0-4-2=-7\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $U$ is not an orthogonal set.

- For the set $V,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=2+0-2=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $V$ is orthogonal.

- For the set $W,$ notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=-18+18=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $W$ is orthogonal.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$V$ and $W$ only".
